notes: Modified cash basis village (recorded as cash, as FY2023/FY2024). Governmental lines from the Statement of Revenues, Expenditures, and Changes in Fund Balances - Cash Basis, Total Governmental Funds 2022 column (p6; labels and major fund columns p5). Taxes 371,765 split from the General Fund schedule (p10: Property tax 355,951 + Motor vehicle tax 15,814). Intergovernmental revenues 168,777 split from the fund schedules (p10-11: Highway allocation 81,148, Motor vehicle fees 5,912, Homestead allocation 9,468, Other 72,249). Bond proceeds 1,175,000 (Street fund) printed under Other financing sources -> debt_proceeds; bond issue costs, principal and interest printed there -> other_financing (as FY2024). Transfers 29,212 in = out (General to Street 5,988 and Fire 23,224); no proprietary transfers. Beginning/ending cash = total assets of governmental funds (all cash: 2021 comparative 1,981,149 and 2022 2,436,895, p4), equal to fund balances. Business-type (Water and Sewer combined, no per-fund statement) from the proprietary Statement of Revenues, Expenditures and Changes in Net Position (p8; modified cash basis with capital assets, depreciation and debt, measure net position); disbursements total = operating 293,754 + non-operating 98,644 (the Statement of Activities p2 shows 346,877 business-type expenses, with bond issue costs 45,521 among general revenues). Proprietary cash flow statement (p9) printed but proprietary left null as in later years (non-GAAP). Balance sheet: government-wide Statement of Net Position (p1), since it includes capital assets and debt. Detail: per-fund statements for the major funds (p10-11) and non-major funds (p13; Fire Fund and Keno-Special Revenue), plus the proprietary Schedule 6 Actual column (p16); zero lines omitted. Schedule 5 (p15) prints only fund-type budget totals and is not recorded. Trim lacks Exhibits D/F (reconciliations), not needed. Read pages 1-16 of 16
